edges.description: Accumulated methylmalonate is excreted in urine, the marker of the mitochondrial arm.
Methylmalonate and propionate pathway intermediates are toxic to mitochondrial energy metabolism, but the step from metabolite to the specific neurological lesion is not established.
Accumulated homocysteine spills into plasma and urine, the marker of the cytosolic arm.

edges.description: Reports loss of adenosylcobalamin-dependent methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity.
Low methionine alongside high homocysteine localises the block to remethylation rather than transsulfuration.

nodes.description: The mitochondrial coenzyme is not made, so methylmalonyl-CoA mutase has no cofactor.

Prolonged fasting and dehydration precipitate decompensation in the methylmalonate-affected forms. Nitrous oxide is singled out because it irreversibly oxidises the cobalamin cofactor of methionine synthase, so it attacks the same step the disease already impairs - a routine anesthetic that is specifically hazardous here.
nodes.id: Avoidance of Catabolic Stress and Nitrous Oxide

evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Prolonged fasting (longer than overnight without dextrose-containing intravenous fluids); dietary protein intake below the recommended dietary allowance for age or more than that prescribed by a metabolic specialist; methionine restriction including use of medical foods that do not contain methionine; and the anesthetic nitrous oxide.

nodes.description: Provides an alternative, methionine-synthase-independent route for remethylating homocysteine, so it addresses the cytosolic arm specifically. Relevant to the homocysteine-affected forms and not to isolated cblD-MMA.

evidence.snippet: Long-term management focuses on improving the metabolic derangement by lowering plasma tHcy and MMA concentrations and maintaining plasma methionine concentrations within the normal range.

nodes.description: Missense substitutions in the conserved C-terminal domain disable the region needed for methylcobalamin synthesis while leaving the protein able to support the mitochondrial arm, giving isolated homocystinuria.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of functional domains of the cblD (MMADHC) gene product.
evidence.snippet: Testing 20 mutations (15 missense and five C-terminal truncations) across p.P154-S287 revealed the presence of a region (p.R197-D226) responsible for MeCbl synthesis

genetic_context.allele_type: missense in the conserved C-terminal region

nodes.description: Premature stops across the C-terminus remove the C-terminal domain from every product, so neither arm is served and both coenzymes are deficient.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of functional domains of the cblD (MMADHC) gene product.
evidence.snippet: Previously we have shown that in cblD patients three types of MMADHC mutations exist: 1) null mutations N-terminal to Met116 cause isolated methylmalonic aciduria (cblD-MMA) due to AdoCbl deficiency; 2) null mutations across the C-terminus (p.Y140-R250) cause combined methylmalonic aciduria and homocystinuria (cblD-MMA/HC) due to AdoCbl and MeCbl deficiency; 3) missense mutations in a conserved C-terminal region (p.D246-L259) cause isolated homocystinuria (cblD-HC) due to MeCbl deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms leading to three different phenotypes in the cblD defect of intracellular cobalamin metabolism.
evidence.snippet: In cblD-MMA/HC cells, improving mitochondrial targeting of MMADHC clearly increased the formation of adenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl) with a concomitant decrease in MeCbl formation.

genetic_context.allele_type: nonsense or frameshift across the C-terminus (p.Y140-R250)

nodes.description: Developmental delay and cognitive deficits are reported across the biochemical forms.

evidence.reference_title: MMADHC premature termination codons in the pathogenesis of cobalamin D disorder: Potential of translational readthrough reconstitution.
evidence.snippet: CblD patients present methylmalonic aciduria (MMA), homocystinuria (HC), or combined MMA/HC, and usually suffer developmental delay and cognitive deficits.

nodes.description: Homocysteine rises while methionine and therefore S-adenosylmethionine fall, so methylation-dependent processes and one-carbon metabolism are both impaired.
Elevated total plasma homocysteine, the biochemical marker of the cytosolic arm. It defines the isolated homocystinuria form and is also present in the combined form.

evidence.reference_title: The cblD defect causes either isolated or combined deficiency of methylcobalamin and adenosylcobalamin synthesis.
evidence.snippet: Two patients presented with isolated homocystinuria

nodes.description: Reduced tone, part of the neurologic presentation of this group of disorders.

evidence.snippet: global developmental delay, encephalopathy, and neurologic signs such as hypotonia and seizures

nodes.description: Blocked remethylation traps folate and impairs thymidylate and purine synthesis, so DNA synthesis in erythroid precursors lags nuclear maturation - the mechanism shared with the other remethylation disorders.

nodes.description: In the cytosol MMADHC takes cobalamin from MMACHC and passes it toward methionine synthase. When that function is lost, methylcobalamin is not made.
nodes.id: Loss of Cytosolic Cobalamin Routing to Methionine Synthase

evidence.reference_title: Mitochondrial depolarization stabilizes the vitamin B(12) chaperone MMADHC in the cytosol to increase MTR activity.
evidence.snippet: Cytosol-stabilized MMADHC increases MTR levels and activity.

nodes.description: MMADHC normally sends part of the processed cobalamin into mitochondria for adenosylcobalamin synthesis. When that function is lost, MMAB is not supplied. That MMADHC is needed for this step is established; how it hands cobalamin on inside the organelle is not (see the cbld_mitochondrial_function_unknown discussion).

evidence.reference_title: Subcellular location of MMACHC and MMADHC, two human proteins central to intracellular vitamin B(12) metabolism.
evidence.snippet: We show that MMACHC is cytoplasmic while MMADHC is both mitochondrial and cytoplasmic

evidence.reference_title: Gene identification for the cblD defect of vitamin B12 metabolism.
evidence.snippet: The cblD gene was localized to human chromosome 2q23.2, and a candidate gene, designated MMADHC (methylmalonic aciduria, cblD type, and homocystinuria), was identified in this region.

evidence.reference_title: Gene identification for the cblD defect of vitamin B12 metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Transfection of wild-type MMADHC rescued the cellular phenotype, and the functional importance of mutant alleles was shown by means of transfection with mutant constructs.

nodes.description: Macrocytic anemia with megaloblastic marrow. Occurs wherever remethylation fails, which is both the isolated homocystinuria form and the combined form.

evidence.snippet: cytopenias (including megaloblastic anemia), global developmental delay, encephalopathy, and neurologic signs such as hypotonia and seizures

nodes.description: The cytosolic coenzyme is not made, so methionine synthase cannot remethylate homocysteine to methionine.
Methylmalonyl-CoA and methylmalonate build up, with the metabolic decompensation risk of an organic acidemia during catabolic stress.
Elevated methylmalonic acid, the biochemical marker of the mitochondrial arm. It defines the isolated methylmalonic aciduria form and is also present in the combined form.

evidence.reference_title: The cblD defect causes either isolated or combined deficiency of methylcobalamin and adenosylcobalamin synthesis.
evidence.snippet: one patient with isolated methylmalonic aciduria and deficient adenosylcobalamin synthesis in fibroblasts, defined as cblD-variant 2

readouts.interpretation: Reports loss of adenosylcobalamin-dependent methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity.

nodes.description: Premature stops early in the coding sequence remove the N-terminal segment, between Met62 and Met116, that adenosylcobalamin synthesis needs. Reinitiation downstream yields a shorter protein that keeps the cytosolic function, which is why these patients have isolated methylmalonic aciduria.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms leading to three different phenotypes in the cblD defect of intracellular cobalamin metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, our data indicate that the sequence after Met116 is sufficient for MeCbl synthesis, whereas the additional sequence between Met62 and Met116 is required for AdoCbl synthesis.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms leading to three different phenotypes in the cblD defect of intracellular cobalamin metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Accordingly, western blot studies reveal proteins of the size expected from the stop codon position with subsequent reinitiation of translation.

genetic_context.allele_type: nonsense or frameshift N-terminal to Met116

nodes.description: Developmental delay, cognitive deficits and seizures. PROVISIONAL because both arms are implicated and the entry does not claim to resolve which metabolite does the damage in any individual patient.

The mainstay. Supplying cobalamin in excess can drive residual flux through whichever arm retains partial function; it is given by injection because the defect is in intracellular handling rather than absorption.

evidence.snippet: Early institution of injectable hydroxocobalamin improves survival and may reduce but not completely prevent primary manifestations.

readouts.interpretation: Low methionine alongside high homocysteine localises the block to remethylation rather than transsulfuration.
